extracted.intended_audience: authors, journal editors, and peer reviewers of health research
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on choosing and correctly applying reporting guidelines when writing and publishing health research to ensure clear, transparent, and useful reports across many study types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose and correctly apply appropriate reporting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for Reporting Health Research is a practical guide to choosing and correctly applying the appropriate guidelines when reporting health research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the reporting guideline that matches the study design and follow it when writing the manuscript to ensure completeness and transparency. The manual provides chapters and examples to help choose and apply the right guideline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent reporting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should be transparent so readers can understand what was done and why; transparency is a core purpose of reporting guidelines and is emphasised throughout the manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of good reporting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The manual describes the characteristics of good reporting guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the chapter on characteristics for guidance on what makes a guideline useful (how it is developed, clarity, scope, applicability). The manual discusses these features rather than listing them exhaustively on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to use reporting guidelines when writing health research
rubrics_metrics.description: How to effectively use reporting guidelines when writing about health research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical advice on integrating guideline checklists into manuscript preparation so reports are clear and complete; includes examples and suggestions in the manual chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish reporting from conduct
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting guidelines guide what information to include in a report; they do not by themselves indicate whether the study conduct was appropriate. Authors should report conduct transparently and reviewers/editors should understand this distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide illustrative examples of good and bad reporting (and conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use examples that illustrate good and bad reporting versus good and bad conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual includes example pairs to show common reporting failings and how they differ from methodological flaws, to help authors and reviewers recognise and fix reporting problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report statistical analyses clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: How to report statistical analyses within research manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapters discuss best practices for describing statistical methods and results so readers can judge analyses; includes tips and example wording (see manual chapters on statistics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Present figures and clinical images appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Tips for the presentation of figures and clinical images in scientific manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance covers labelling, legends, image quality, and ethical considerations for clinical images to ensure clarity and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a reporting guidelines policy in journals
rubrics_metrics.description: How to establish a reporting guidelines policy in your health journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual provides advice for editors and publishers on adopting and implementing reporting guideline policies, including which guidelines to endorse and how to enforce them during peer review and production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use CONSORT for randomised trials (and extensions)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply CONSORT checklist and relevant CONSORT extensions when reporting randomized controlled trials to ensure essential trial details are reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use STROBE for observational studies (and extensions)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use STROBE and its extensions to report cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies completely and transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use PRISMA for systematic reviews (and extensions)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow PRISMA checklists (and extensions where applicable) to report review methods and results clearly, including search strategies, selection processes, and synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use SPIRIT and PRISMA-P for study protocols
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register and report trial and review protocols using SPIRIT (for protocols of clinical trials) and PRISMA-P (for protocols of systematic reviews) to improve transparency of planned methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use STARD and TRIPOD for diagnostic/prognostic studies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report diagnostic accuracy studies and prognostic model studies using STARD and TRIPOD guidance respectively to ensure reproducible and interpretable results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use CARE for case reports (and extensions)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow CARE checklist to ensure key case information and learning points are reported; consider any CARE extensions relevant to specific case types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AGREE and RIGHT for clinical practice guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical practice guidelines: AGREE and RIGHT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AGREE and RIGHT tools to develop and report trustworthy clinical practice guidelines, covering methodology, stakeholder involvement, and presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use SRQR and COREQ for qualitative research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply SRQR or COREQ checklists when reporting qualitative studies to ensure transparency in sampling, data collection, analysis, and researcher reflexivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ARRIVE for animal pre-clinical studies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow ARRIVE guidelines to report animal experiments thoroughly, including ethical approvals, housing, randomisation, blinding, and outcome measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use SQUIRE for quality improvement studies (and extensions)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report quality improvement work using SQUIRE to describe context, interventions, measures, and generalisability; consult extensions for specific designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use CHEERS for economic evaluations (and extensions)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply CHEERS checklist to report reporting of economic evaluations, including perspective, time horizon, costs, and sensitivity analyses.
